quotes.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately.
Only that day dawns to which we are awake.
Things do not change; we change.
Love your life, poor as it is.
However mean your life is, meet it and live it.
Rise free from care before the dawn, and seek adventures.
We must learn to reawaken and keep ourselves awake, not by mechanical aids, but by an infinite expectation of the dawn.
Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
Insist on yourself; never imitate.
The years teach much which the days never know.
Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year.
Hitch your wagon to a star.
Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if thou wilt ever dig.
Be like the promontory against which the waves continually break, but it stands firm.
Confine thyself to the present.
No longer talk at all about the kind of man that a good man ought to be, but be such.
In the morning when thou risest unwillingly, let this thought be present: I am rising to the work of a human being.
If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgement about it.
Nowhere either with more quiet or more freedom from trouble does a man retire than into his own soul.
Hold every hour in your grasp.
Lay hold of to-day's task, and you will not need to depend so much upon to-morrow's.
We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
You need a change of soul rather than a change of climate.
When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.
Of things some are in our power, and others are not.
Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.
No great thing is produced suddenly, since not even the grape or the fig is.
I travel not to go anywhere, but to go. I travel for travel's sake. The great affair is to move.
Lose no time; be always employ'd in something useful.

lines: "Hope" is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -
poems.title: Hope is the thing with feathers

lines: I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
poems.title: I wandered lonely as a cloud

lines: They flash upon that inward eye
Which is the bliss of solitude;
poems.title: I wandered lonely as a cloud

lines: While with an eye made quiet by the power
Of harmony, and the deep power of joy,
We see into the life of things.
poems.title: Tintern Abbey

lines: Come forth into the light of things,
Let Nature be your teacher.
poems.title: The tables turned

lines: My heart leaps up when I behold
A rainbow in the sky:
poems.title: My heart leaps up

lines: Ne'er saw I, never felt, a calm so deep!
poems.title: Composed upon Westminster Bridge

lines: Afoot and light-hearted I take to the open road,
Healthy, free, the world before me,
The long brown path before me leading wherever I choose.
poems.title: Song of the open road

lines: Henceforth I ask not good-fortune, I myself am good-fortune,
poems.title: Song of the open road

lines: I believe a leaf of grass is no less than the journey-work of the stars,
poems.title: Song of myself

lines: I exist as I am, that is enough,
poems.title: Song of myself

lines: Look'd up in perfect silence at the stars.
poems.title: When I heard the learn'd astronomer

lines: Does the road wind up-hill all the way?
Yes, to the very end.
Will the day's journey take the whole long day?
From morn to night, my friend.
poems.title: Up-hill

lines: My heart is like a singing bird
poems.title: A birthday

lines: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever:
Its loveliness increases; it will never
Pass into nothingness;
poems.title: Endymion

lines: If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
poems.title: Ode to the west wind

lines: To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower,
Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand
And Eternity in an hour.
poems.title: Auguries of innocence

lines: Two roads diverged in a wood, and I-
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.
poems.title: The road not taken

lines: The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep,
And miles to go before I sleep,
poems.title: Stopping by woods on a snowy evening

lines: To strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield.
poems.title: Ulysses

lines: For men may come and men may go,
But I go on for ever.
poems.title: The brook

lines: I am the master of my fate,
I am the captain of my soul.
poems.title: Invictus

lines: Let us, then, be up and doing,
With a heart for any fate;
Still achieving, still pursuing,
Learn to labor and to wait.
poems.title: A psalm of life

lines: The world is so full of a number of things,
I'm sure we should all be as happy as kings.
poems.title: Happy thought

lines: And I shall have some peace there, for peace comes dropping slow,
poems.title: The lake isle of Innisfree

lines: I must go down to the seas again, to the lonely sea and the sky,
And all I ask is a tall ship and a star to steer her by;
poems.title: Sea-fever

lines: The year's at the spring
And day's at the morn;
Morning's at seven;
The hill-side's dew-pearled;
poems.title: Pippa passes

lines: If you can wait and not be tired by waiting,
poems.title: If-

lines: Life has loveliness to sell,
All beautiful and splendid things,
poems.title: Barter

lines: I will arise and go now, and go to Innisfree,
poems.title: The lake isle of Innisfree
